readme: The queue for the overnight build loop (docs/overnight/PROMPT.md). File order is priority order. status: todo, done or blocked. size: S (about an hour) or M (about half a night); split anything bigger. Every item is also subject to the full gate, `pnpm overnight:check`. Edit by hand or with `node tools/overnight/backlog.mjs`.

items.title: Guard the IP rules with a test
items.why: CLAUDE.md, IP rules (hard): banned names must never ship in code, assets, copy or comments. Nothing checks this today.
acceptance: A unit test scans every tracked text file under apps/, packages/, content/ and assets/ and fails when a term banned by CLAUDE.md's IP rules appears (case-insensitive, whole words): the series abbreviation, its full name, and its publisher's name.
The banned terms are built in the test so that the test file does not itself contain them as plain words.
The test proves it has teeth: it runs the same scanner over a small in-memory sample that contains a banned term and expects a hit.
The test passes on the current tree without editing any shipped file, or the offending text is reworded.
verify: pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/ip-rules.test.ts

items.title: Prove pause-on-background and the free-roam autosave
items.why: CLAUDE.md, Game rules that must hold: pause when the tab or app is backgrounded; autosave every 2 minutes of free roam. Both are implemented in apps/game/src/game.ts and neither has a test.
acceptance: An e2e test makes the page hidden (visibilitychange with document.hidden true), then checks world.time does not advance while hidden and advances again once the page is visible.
The same spec fast-forwards more than 120 s of free roam with the test hook and checks a save has landed in IndexedDB.
The free-roam autosave interval is read from content JSON (validated with Zod) instead of the literal 120 in game.ts (architecture rule 3).
No console errors in the new test.
verify: pnpm exec playwright test -c playwright.config.ts --project=desktop tests/e2e/lifecycle.spec.ts

items.title: Assert the draw-call and triangle budget at the phone's screen size on the mid tier
items.why: CLAUDE.md, Performance budget: under 100 draw calls and about 100k visible vertices on a mid-range phone. tests/perf/drawcalls.spec.ts only measures the high tier at a 960x540 desktop size.
acceptance: tests/perf has a test that loads `?autostart=1&quality=mid` at a 956x440 viewport, populates the scene as drawcalls.spec.ts does (HEAT 3, traffic, people) and asserts the maximum draw calls stay under 100.

The same test logs the maximum triangle count and asserts it stays under a budget written in the test with a comment giving the measured value on the day it was added (budget no more than 1.5x the measurement).
`pnpm perf` passes and takes no more than 30 s longer than before.
verify: pnpm perf

items.title: Make the phone test's steal step deterministic
items.why: docs/STATUS.md (Side activities, Open): the `phone.spec` steal step failed in 2 of 3 full-suite runs; the player was FLATLINED on foot after being teleported beside a traffic car. Cause not pinned down.
acceptance: The cause is identified and written into docs/STATUS.md (replacing the open note).
The Hot Chrome phone test passes 5 times in a row in each orientation.
The fix does not delete or shorten the steal step and does not add retries; if the cause is a real game bug (a stunned car still running the player over, say) it is fixed in the sim with a unit test.
verify: pnpm exec playwright test -c playwright.config.ts --project=iphone-portrait --project=iphone-landscape -g 'Hot Chrome' --repeat-each=5

items.title: Player horn
items.why: docs/STATUS.md (Sound, Open): there is no player horn input yet; the audio layer already plays `horn` events.
acceptance: A `horn` intent exists in packages/sim/src/intents.ts and is fed by keyboard (H), gamepad and a touch button of at least 48 px that shows only while driving.
While the player drives, the intent makes the sim emit a `horn` event, rate-limited by a value in content JSON; unit-tested in Node.
Pedestrians within a radius from content JSON ahead of the car step aside; unit-tested.
The phone test asserting touch buttons stay on screen and at least 48 px still passes with the new button, and the audio e2e reports no errors.
verify: pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/vehicle.test.ts tests/unit/living-city.test.ts
pnpm exec playwright test -c playwright.config.ts --project=iphone-landscape -g '48 px'

items.title: TRACE at 100 % tags the player: a HEAT 2 floor
items.why: docs/DESIGN.md (HEAT and TRACE) and docs/STATUS.md (Cut, and why): TRACE rises and decays but nothing reacts to it.
acceptance: At TRACE 100 the player is tagged: HEAT cannot decay below 2 while tagged. The floor and the thresholds live in content/data/heat.json, validated with Zod.
The tag clears when TRACE has decayed below a release value from the same JSON, after which HEAT decays normally.
The HUD shows a TAGGED state beside the TRACE read-out (text plus shape, not colour alone).
Unit tests cover: tagged at 100, floor holds through a full decay period out of sight, release, and no effect below 100.
verify: pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/heat.test.ts tests/unit/wanted.test.ts

items.title: Shop sign posts are physical
items.why: docs/STATUS.md (Economy, Known gaps): the kerbside sign posts have no colliders, so cars drive through them.
acceptance: Each kerbside shop sign post is a breakable prop in the sim (like street lamps in packages/sim/src/street.ts), with its smash speed and speed loss in content/data/props.json.
A unit test drives a car into a sign post below and above the smash speed and checks it stops or smashes accordingly.
Draw calls do not rise: `pnpm perf` still passes.
No new draws on the main city RNG (docs/STATUS.md): mission-lint stays clean.
verify: pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/props.test.ts tests/unit/kerbs.test.ts
pnpm mission-lint
pnpm perf

items.title: Hostile crew cars chase the player on their turf
items.why: docs/STATUS.md (Living city, Open): hostile crew cars cruise but do not chase.
acceptance: A crew car whose crew's respect for the player is at or below the hostile threshold, on its own turf and within a sight range from content/data/life.json, switches to pursuit using the existing actor driver behaviours.
It gives up beyond a leash distance or after a time limit, both from life.json, and returns to cruising.
Ram damage uses the same capped, rate-limited rule as police and squads (heat.json `ramDamage`).
Unit tests cover: neutral crew cars never chase, hostile ones do, and the leash.
verify: pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/living-city.test.ts
